x: Church tools keep asking people for the same details. Lookup fills them in from Here's My Church, an open directory of 587,842 churches in 19 countries. Someone types a few letters, picks their church, and the address, website, phone and service times fill in.

- Quickstart: Add the search box to a form in a few minutes, or hand the job to your agent. - Example apps: A church management app, a nonprofit sign-up and a church website builder. - The widget: Every attribute, event and form option, with a live preview. - API: Search and church records over plain HTTP, with open CORS and no key.

1. Search as you type. Prefixes, typos and places like "church in dallas" all work, nearby churches first. 2. Fill your form. Pick a church and the empty fields you tagged with data-hmc-field fill in. Anything already typed is left alone. 3. Share fixes back. When someone corrects a detail Lookup filled, they can share it back to Here's My Church, one checked box at a time. Because every pick comes from the same open directory, each app that uses Lookup helps keep church data accurate.

- Here's My Church, the open, crowd-sourced church directory every result comes from. - OpenStreetMap contributors, whose map data many listings started from (ODbL). - Cam Pak and Sensible UI. The widget reads the same design token names Sensible UI uses, so it fits right in on those pages. Lookup was built for the AI for Church hackathon and is open source on GitHub.
Add Lookup to your app Or set it up yourself. There's no key to request.

It's a real form field. Give it a name and the chosen church's ID submits with your form, so you can store the ID and look the church up again later. React and Vue get types for the tag and its events. html form: react:

Fields named for the church fill without any setup: churchcity, churchWebsite, churchphone, or autocomplete="section-church address-level2". It reads the field's name, id and autocomplete, and skips address line 2, hidden fields and passwords. On a form that's only about the church, add fill="auto" and plain names fill too: city, state, zip, phone, email, website, or autocomplete tokens like postal-code and tel. A plain name or id never fills, since on most forms those are the person's. To say exactly which field gets what, tag it with data-hmc-field. A tag always wins, and data-hmc-field="none" leaves a field alone. Use any of these: name, street, city, region, regionName, postalCode, country, countryName, latitude, longitude, phone, email, website, denomination, serviceTimes, languages, ministries, pastorName and id. A <select fills when one of its options matches by value or text, as a code or a name: TX or Texas, US or United States. For fields outside the form, set the fieldMap property to a field name and an element or selector each:

After a fill, changing a field Lookup filled shows the changes below the church field, checked, with Share N fixes. Street, city and postal code show as one Address row. "Still correct?" appears only for listings nobody confirmed in the last year. See Data and review for what's accepted where.

To let people share as part of submitting your form, add a checkbox with data-hmc-share. If it's checked when the form submits, the checked changes are sent in the background (with keepalive, so leaving the page doesn't cut them off). The submit is never delayed or blocked.

When nothing matches, the "Add it" link opens Here's My Church's add form with the typed name. If someone fills in your form without picking a church, the widget offers to add it, listing the values it would send from your mapped fields (it needs a name, city and region). Similar listings come first as "Is it one of these?"; picking one selects it. Once added, the widget's value is the new church's ID.

Use the icons your design system already has. Put one with slot="search-icon" in the box, and one with slot="result-icon" to repeat beside every result. It works with SVG sets like Lucide or Heroicons, icon fonts like Tabler or Font Awesome, and icon components like Iconify, because the icons stay in your page and pick up its CSS.

Event · When it fires · church-results · Results appeared. detail has query, results, settled, and more when they came from Show more. · church-select · A church was chosen. Cancel it to stop the fill. · church-fill · Fields are about to fill. Cancel it to fill them yourself from detail.record. · church-clear · The choice was cleared, with the clear button or by editing the name. · church-error · A search or a church's details failed to load. detail has query or id, plus status, code, retryAfter and the error. · church-contribute · Someone chose Share, reported a problem, or submitted with data-hmc-share checked (detail.onSubmit). detail has churchId and changes; an address change's value is { street, city, postalCode }. Cancel it to send them yourself, or not at all. · church-confirm · Someone chose Still correct. Cancel it to skip the confirmation. · church-add · Someone chose to add a church that isn't listed. detail has church and confirmAdd. Cancel it to stop the add. · church-added · A church was added. detail has its new id (null with lookup-demo), the church and sandbox. The widget's value is already the new ID. ·

An ARIA 1.2 combobox: arrow keys move through results, Enter chooses and Escape closes. Show more is the last option, so the arrow keys reach it too, and pressing down on it loads the next page. Results, added results and fills are announced, targets are 44 pixels, and it respects forced colors and reduced motion.

It shows only fields Here's My Church accepts for that church's country. Changed fields start checked, street, city and postalCode show as one Address row, each says whether it goes live or waits for a moderator, and nothing is sent until the person chooses Share. A checked data-hmc-share checkbox in the submitted form sends them too, without blocking the submit. When nothing changed, it asks "Still correct?" of listings nobody confirmed this year. It also offers Report a problem and a link to fix anything else on Here's My Church.

Wrap a service-times field in <church-service-times to edit it as rows of day, time and label, the same way Here's My Church does. The field keeps one plain string, such as Sun 9:00 AM (Main Service); Wed 7:00 PM, so it submits like any input. When <church-lookup fills a serviceTimes field inside <church-service-times, the rows update with it.

When one isn't set, it falls back to the shadcn/ui token names (--background, --foreground, --accent, --border, --radius and so on), the same names Sensible UI by Cam Pak uses. Base URL https://lookup.heresmychurch.com/v1. Open CORS, no key, no cookies. Send a client name, such as your app's, so Here's My Church knows which tool is asking.

Try it against the live API: · Parameter · What it does · q · What the person typed. Place words like "in Dallas" or ", TX" are understood. · near, lat, lng · Rank near a place or point. · country, region · Only return churches there. · limit · 1 to 50. Defaults to 8. · settled=1 · The person paused, so semantic search may run. · geo=off · Don't use the request's approximate location. · The response has results, plus hasMore when more churches ranked past limit. To show more, ask again with a higher limit and add the results you haven't shown yet. A higher limit can search wider, so don't assume the first ones come back in the same order. It also has place (the place understood from the query, or null), corrected (the spelling searched instead, or null), degraded and semantic.

The autofill record. Every key in fields is always present, with null or when empty, plus missing, completeness, hints, freshness.lastVerified (when someone last confirmed it, in milliseconds, or null) and links.heresMyChurch (the church's page; add ?suggest=1 to open its fix form). Records are cached for a minute, and a change that goes live through Lookup refreshes it at once.
Field names, what can be contributed and how it's reviewed (contributableFields), whether adding churches is on (addEnabled), completeness weights, counts and attribution.

Send corrections as { client, changes: { field, value } }. Fields are serviceTimes, denomination, languages, ministries, phone, website, email, pastorName, the address, and the reports reportClosed, reportDuplicate and reportRelocated. Send an address as { "field": "address", "value": { "street", "city", "postalCode" } } (any of the three), or as separate street, city and postalCode changes; either way it goes to Here's My Church as one change, and parts you leave out keep their listed values. Up to 8 changes at once. Each field comes back with its own status: · Status · Meaning · live · Applied now. These fields go live on one vote. · inreview · Waits for a Here's My Church moderator. · notapplied · Not changed: the listed value was already the same, or Here's My Church kept it. · rejected · Not accepted, with a message saying why. · tryagain · A temporary problem, such as maintenance or a rate limit. Nothing was refused. · comingsoon · A field Lookup will accept soon. Name is coming soon. · Sandbox: Test with client: "lookup-demo". Changes are checked the same way but never sent, and responses say sandbox: true. When a change goes live, the response has updated: true and the reco
"Still correct." Send { client } to mark a listing as checked today. The response has the new lastVerified.

Add a church that isn't listed. Send { client, church }, where church has name, city and region (a code like TX or a name like Texas), and optionally street, postalCode, country (code or name), phone, email, website, denomination, serviceTimes, languages, ministries, pastorName, latitude and longitude. · Status · Meaning · live · Added. id is its new church ID, already searchable. · similar · It may already be listed. similar holds candidates shaped like search results. Send again with confirmAdd: true to add it anyway. · rejected · Not accepted, with a message. · tryagain · A temporary problem. Nothing was added. · With lookup-demo, the duplicate check runs against Lookup's own index and nothing is added: a live answer has id: null and sandbox: true.
Ask a question about these docs. Send { question } (up to 500 characters) and the answer streams back as server-sent events. It powers the Ask AI button and is limited to 10 questions a minute.

Errors are JSON with a readable error and a stable code to check in your code: · Status · code · 400 · invalid · 404 · notfound · 405 · methodnotallowed · 413 · toolarge · 429 · ratelimited · 500 · unavailable · 503 · overloaded ·

120 requests and 30 semantic searches a minute per visitor, 5 contributions (adds included) and 10 docs questions a minute. Over the limit returns 429, a busy database returns 503, and both send Retry-After, which browsers on any origin can read.

1. Words, as you type. A full-text index finds names that start with what's typed: nearby first, then wider, then the whole country. Short forms count too: "1st", "bapt", "meth", "pres", "ch", and abbreviations like "umc", "fbc", "ame", "cogic", "sda" and "lds" match the words they stand for, and the other way round. 2. Places. "church in dallas", "grace, chicago", "first baptist TX" and "first baptist dallas tx" become a place filter. A lowercase state code like "tx" also finds churches in that state, but still works as the start of a word, so "grace co" keeps finding Grace Community. "nyc", "philly", "ft worth" and "n charleston" are understood, and so are postcodes where listings have them, mostly in Europe ("kirche 80331"; US listings don't carry ZIP codes yet). A lowercase "in" is never read as Indiana. 3. Half-typed words and spelling. When almost nothing matches, every word is tried as the start of a longer one, with "church" optional, so "first bap church dallas" finds First Baptist. Then the closest spelling is tried, so "gracee" finds Grace. 4. Meaning, only when words fail. If no result matches every word, a settled query also asks semantic search (bge-m3 in Cloudflare V

78 held-out test queries we didn't tune on, against Here's My Church's search today: · System · Top result right · In top 5 · No results · Typical time · Today's search · 28% · 31% · 41% · 20 s · Lookup, words only · 78% · 85% · 1% · 150 ms · Lookup, with semantic · 78% · 87% · 0% · 170 ms · Semantic search helped two queries in 78 and hurt none. It doesn't fix translations such as "trinity church munich", and common names with no location stay hard. Full write-up.

A formula, not AI, orders results. - When you give a place or a point (a city in the search, or lat/lng), every church that matches all your words competes on one footing: about 40% how well the words match, 30% how near it is, 10% for being in the city you named, a bonus for an exact name, and a little for a complete listing. So "Calvary Chapel West Boca" 28 km away beats an exact "Calvary Chapel" 300 km away. - Otherwise a better name match always comes first, then 60% name, 25% nearness to the visitor's approximate location, and 15% listing completeness.

h: Where AI is used, and where it isn't
x: Where · How · Semantic search · One AI model, bge-m3 on Cloudflare Workers AI and Vectorize, runs only when no name matches every word. On the held-out test it moved "in top 5" from 85% to 87% and "no results" from 1% to 0%. · Ask AI in these docs · An instruct model on Workers AI answers questions using only these docs, and links the pages it used. Questions aren't stored. · Ranking · A formula, not AI. · Church details · AI never writes or changes them. Every fill comes from Here's My Church, and every shared fix goes through its review rules. · Searches · Lookup doesn't log them. ·

Lookup reads Here's My Church's reviewed listings and re-syncs changed regions every 5 minutes. Searches aren't logged, and approximate location is only used in memory to rank nearby churches. Why fewer churches than Here's My Church shows?: Its map counts every listing, about 655,000. Lookup leaves out about 68,000 that have no real name yet, such as "Unnamed church", since nobody can find those by typing. Once a listing gets a name on Here's My Church, the next sync adds it.
